subject.size_in_frame: sitting back on his haunches, about 0.18 of frame height — no closer than sh027's set-up allows, the frame simply loses Alice

headroom: about 0.26 of frame height of brick vault above him. The vault is kept over his head in every frame of this shot so he never reads as free-standing or human-scaled.
horizon_eyeline: Floor line and vault arcs converge as in sh027, vanishing point at [0.52, 0.52]. His eyeline drops to the watch braced against his chest and stays there for the whole shot — it never rises to the lens.

layers.fg: empty wet brick floor and one lamp pool across the bottom of frame; Alice is out of shot entirely
layers.mg: the Rabbit, a small clear silhouette against the lamplight, the dropped gloves between his forefeet
layers.bg: the passage running on past him to the far corner glow

gaze.note: his whole attention is on the watch; he is given no lead room and no space to look back into, because he does not look back. Performance is muzzle, ears and the set of his back only.

balance: A single small subject held dead centre in a long empty corridor. The symmetry is unglamorous and slightly comic — a very small animal taking up the exact middle of a very large room.
leading_lines: The converging vault and floor lines again, all arriving at him. The gloves on the bricks in front of his forefeet are a small pale mark that stops the eye at floor level.
eye_first: The white of his fur against the lamplit brick, then down to the gloves at his feet.
constraint_binding: QUADRUPED RABBIT: he stops and sits back on his haunches with the watch braced in a paw against his chest — the composition never shows him upright on two legs and never frames him from a height that would imply a human stance. Clean single so the native dialogue take has one speaker in frame: Alice is wholly out of the frame for the line.
